bull_bear.body:
- Established brands and strong market positions across three building materials businesses built over three decades, including the pioneer position of H & R Johnson in Indian ceramic tiles
- Extensive distribution ecosystem of dealers, retailers, contractors, architects, influencers, experience centres and channel partners, with a pan-India network of 900+ dealers and 22 experience centres in tiles and bath
- Regional cement leadership in the Satna cluster and across Central India, supported by an average lead distance that reduced to 362 km in 2025-26 from 376 km in 2024-25
- Premiumisation of the portfolio - premium products (Champion Plus, Champion Duratech, Champion All Weather) rose to 54% of cement sales volume in 2025-26 from 42%, and GVT rose to 27% of tiles volume from 25%
- Sustainability-led cost advantage - installed green power capacity including WHRS of 59.5 MW as of March 31, 2026 and an AFR project at the cement plant, with GHG intensity reduced to 598 kg CO2 per tonne
- Headroom for operating leverage - the tiles business operated at around 66.2% capacity utilisation during 2025-26
- Strengthened credit profile - India Ratings reaffirmed the long-term issuer rating at 'IND A+/Positive' and short-term rating at 'IND A1+' during 2025-26
- Diversified product resilience across housing, commercial, industrial and infrastructure construction segments
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Energy costs and GHG emissions — Energy expenditure constitutes a material component of cement manufacturing costs and a significant source of greenhouse gas emissions; escalating energy prices, regulatory momentum toward low-carbon operations and the cement sector's net-zero-by-2070 commitment require sustained efficiency gains and a transition to cleaner energy. Financial implication flagged as negative.
- Water availability and water stress — Water is an essential input across cement, tiles and ready-mixed concrete operations; intensifying water stress, competition for freshwater and heightened regulatory oversight demand structured water stewardship. Mitigated through ZLD across plants under operational control, rainwater harvesting and groundwater recharge.
- Air quality and biodiversity impact of quarrying and manufacturing — Emissions from manufacturing can adversely affect ambient air quality in surrounding areas and expose the Company to regulatory sanctions and reputational consequences, while quarrying and manufacturing can affect local ecosystems and habitats, putting the social licence to operate and evolving disclosure requirements at stake; addressed through CEMS/CAAQMS monitoring, LEAP-based biodiversity risk assessments, TNFD alignment and mine rehabilitation.
- Occupational health and safety — Unsafe working environments expose employees, contractors and workers to injury risks and the Company to regulatory penalties, legal liability and reputational harm; managed through an OHS policy and management system across all sites and periodic risk assessments.
- Talent attraction, retention and labour relations — Inability to attract, develop and retain a skilled workforce can widen capability gaps, dampen productivity and constrain execution of the strategic growth agenda; unresolved labour grievances and inadequate worker engagement can precipitate industrial action and disrupt production continuity.
- Regulatory and statutory compliance, governance, ethics and data protection — Non-adherence to regulatory and statutory obligations can give rise to legal penalties, operational disruptions and loss of stakeholder confidence; breaches of ethical conduct and deficiencies in governance structures can inflict lasting reputational damage and trigger regulatory action; and inadequate data governance and privacy safeguards can result in significant regulatory fines, reputational damage and operational disruption.
- Financial risks - credit, liquidity and market risk — The Company is exposed to credit risk on trade receivables (treated as in default when payments are more than 2 years past due, with an expected credit loss allowance), liquidity risk in meeting financial liabilities as they fall due, and market risk comprising foreign exchange exposure from overseas sales, purchases and foreign currency loans as well as interest rate risk.
- Supply chain and supplier sustainability, including human rights — Unsustainable or unethical supplier conduct - human rights violations, environmental non-compliance or governance failures - can precipitate supply chain disruptions and reputational harm; unaddressed human rights risks in sourcing, contracting and employment can erode stakeholder trust and attract regulatory scrutiny.

business.body: Prism Johnson Limited manufactures and sells Portland cement and clinker, ceramic tiles, sanitaryware and bath fittings, and ready-mixed concrete, operating through three businesses - Prism Cement, H & R Johnson (India) and Prism RMC. Prism Cement is a prominent player in the Satna cluster serving Madhya Pradesh, Eastern and Central Uttar Pradesh and Bihar; H & R Johnson is a pioneer of ceramic tiles in India selling through a pan-India dealer network; and Prism RMC is one of the top four RMC players in India catering to mega infrastructure projects and urban residential needs. The Company primarily serves a diverse customer base comprising dealers, infrastructure companies, real estate firms and individual homeowners, across housing, commercial, industrial and infrastructure construction segments.

- **Ready-Mix Concrete (Prism RMC):** Ready-mixed concrete, Construction chemicals

outlook.body:
- Maintain financial discipline, deleveraging, cost optimisation and operational excellence to strengthen the balance sheet and long-term competitiveness
- Strategic portfolio realignment - divest the entire 51% stake in Raheja QBE General Insurance to QBE Group to unlock value and sharpen focus on the core building materials businesses
- Premiumisation in cement - grow the share of premium products (Champion Plus, Champion Duratech, Champion All Weather), which reached 54% of cement sales volume in 2025-26
- Deeper regional market penetration in Central India through expansion of the premium and differentiated product portfolio, strengthening of trade channels and enhanced engagement with dealers, contractors, influencers and masons
- Premium and differentiated products in tiles - grow the GVT share of tiles sales volume, which rose to 27% in 2025-26 from 25%
- In RMC, a more disciplined project selection strategy in Mega Projects following the business-model transition, and a higher share of value-added products in Commercial Concrete (29% in 2025-26 from 19%)
- Direct capital expenditure to plant maintenance, modernisation, sustainability initiatives such as Alternative Fuels and Raw Materials (AFR), and operational efficiency improvements across Cement, Tiles, Bathware and RMC
- Disciplined capital allocation with focus on working capital management and free cash flow generation
- The Board has adopted a Dividend Distribution Policy as part of its suite of governance policies, alongside a Related Party Transactions Policy, Policy on Material Subsidiaries and Risk Management Policy, all subject to regular review and periodic revision. For funding, the AGM notice places before shareholders a special resolution for the private placement of non-convertible debentures and/or other debt securities under Sections 42 and 71 of the Companies Act, 2013 and the applicable SEBI regulations.
- Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) status maintained across all cement, tiles and ready-mixed concrete plants under the Company's operational control, with rainwater harvesting and systematic groundwater recharge programmes across plant locations, reducing freshwater withdrawal intensity while increasing recycled water use
- Co-processing of industrial and municipal waste as alternative fuels across cement plants, with the share of renewable energy and Waste Heat Recovery Systems in the overall energy mix being continuously expanded
- Progressive reduction of the clinker-to-cement ratio through substitution of alternative low-carbon raw materials, and energy efficiency improvement programmes across all manufacturing operations
- 32.7% green power - solar and WHRS contribution to the power needs of Prism Cement
- Application of the 4R framework (Reduce, Reuse, Recycle, Recover) across operations, with industrial by-products and waste streams from other industries used as substitute raw materials and alternative fuels; hazardous and non-hazardous waste routed through SPCB-authorised recyclers
- Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (CEMS) and Continuous Ambient Air Quality Monitoring Systems (CAAQMS) installed and operational at manufacturing facilities, with programmes to reduce particulate matter and non-GHG air pollutants
- Biodiversity Risk Assessments using the LEAP approach and a structured Biodiversity Management Programme at Prism Cement, with disclosures being aligned to TNFD recommendations, green belt development, annual plantation drives and active mine rehabilitation programmes at quarrying locations
- Formal Human Rights Policy with human rights due diligence across operations and supply chain, an accessible grievance mechanism, and SA 8000 certification obtained and maintained at Prism Cement
- Supplier Code of Conduct and Sustainable Procurement Policy governing supplier selection and onboarding, with structured Supplier Sustainability Assessments for critical and high-risk suppliers
- #2 NSE ESG Ranking among leading cement companies
- AI-based ACORN Project optimising concrete mix designs and decarbonisation initiatives
- Social performance in 2025-26 - 18 villages benefitted through community development initiatives, Rs 0.8 Crores CSR spend, and 700+ safety trainings for employees and workers at Prism Cement
- Certified management systems - ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015, ISO 45001:2018 and ISO 50001:2018, plus GreenPro, GRIHA, IGBC, QCI and NABL accreditations
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: H & R Johnson operates a diversified manufacturing footprint across India comprising approximately 64 million square metres of annual tile manufacturing capacity across 11 plants, complemented by dedicated facilities for sanitaryware, faucets and specialised industrial products; plant locations are Samba and Baddi (faucets) in the North, Morbi (four tiles plants and one sanitaryware plant), Pen (tiles), Dewas (tiles and IPNR) in the West, Vijayawada (two tiles plants), Kunigal and Karaikal in the South, and Panagarh in the East. The division's stated expansion approach is capacity optimisation and manufacturing modernisation - strategic upgrades at various plants to improve regional supply responsiveness and manufacturing efficiencies, alongside continued plant rationalisation and operational optimisation to lift capacity utilisation, which stood at 66% in 2025-26, and overall cost competitiveness; growth in non-tile businesses is being pursued by leveraging the core tiles distribution network while expanding dedicated bathware channels. The Company's Journey of Growth records the 2020s expansion steps: commissioning of 22.5 MW WHRS and an additional 24 MW of solar power capacity at Satna; a new manufacturing facility for IPNR products at Dewas; expansion of tile production capacity by 5.2 MSM through JV entities and the establishment of a new 6.3 MSM tiles manufacturing plant at Panagarh (WB); installation of a 600 TPD AFR firing system at Satna; completion of modernisation of the tiles plant at Vijayawada; acquisition of a 50% stake in Sunbath Sanitary; bagging of four limestone mine blocks in Satna; NCLT approval for amalgamation with wholly-owned subsidiaries; and an agreement to divest the non-core asset Raheja QBE. Earlier phases had established the cement platform at Satna (first line of 2 MTPA, second line of 3.6 MTPA) and an 8.5 MW solar plant at Satna. The BRSR reports that 31% of capital expenditure in 2025-26 was directed to technologies improving environmental and social impacts, towards construction, modernisation, expansion and upgradation.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Indian cement demand grew approximately 8.6% year-on-year to 491.4 million tonnes in the year (ICRA), and cement volume is projected to increase 7-8% in 2026-27 supported by continued investments in infrastructure, housing and industrial development
- Government infrastructure-led development agenda reinforced by a record capital expenditure allocation of Rs 12.2 Lakh Crores in Union Budget 2026-27, providing long-term demand visibility
- Reduction in GST on cement from 28% to 18% during 2025-26 is expected to improve affordability and strengthen demand
- Rural growth drivers - favourable monsoon, higher farm incomes, rising rural wages and government initiatives such as PMAY-Gramin, rural housing and village infrastructure development
- Urbanisation, household formation and residential and commercial real estate activity supporting long-term cement consumption
- Sustained infrastructure spending on roads, railways, irrigation, urban infrastructure, industrial projects, warehousing and logistics
- Industry shift towards premium, value-added products as homeowners, developers and infrastructure projects prioritise durability and lifecycle cost over initial expense
- Operating environment shaped by industry consolidation in cement, elevated energy costs for the tiles business and working capital pressure in the RMC business
- Rising global energy volatility towards the end of 2025-26 created emerging cost pressures for the sector; volatility in fuel, freight, imported raw material and currency costs remains a key challenge
- Industry-wide adoption of blended cement, renewable energy, WHRS and alternative fuels to reduce carbon emissions and improve efficiency
- India's macro backdrop - real GDP growth estimated at 7.7% in 2025-26 with the RBI projecting approximately 6.9% for 2026-27, aided by lower borrowing costs following 50 bps of repo rate cuts
- The Mega Projects order book stood at approximately 1.4 mn cubic metres at the end of the year
- Following completion of the business-model transition, the Mega Projects business witnessed strong sequential quarterly growth, supported by a robust project pipeline and a more disciplined project selection strategy

deepdive.thesis: A trusted, diversified building materials company with a strong presence across Cement, Tiles and Ready-mix Concrete, and a prominent regional cement player in Central India.

open.item: The Company has entered into an agreement to divest its entire 51% stake in Raheja QBE General Insurance Company Limited to its joint venture partner QBE Group, to sharpen focus on the core building materials portfolio and reduce debt.
Prism Cement is implementing its Alternative Fuel and Raw Material (AFR) project, with the AFR firing system upgraded and debottlenecked during the year to enable higher AFR utilisation.

Prism Johnson has entered into an agreement to divest its entire 51% stake in Raheja QBE General Insurance Company Limited to QBE Group, with divestment proceeds of Rs 324 Crores subject to standard post-closing adjustments.
The Company intends to continue strengthening its balance sheet through improved operating performance, healthy internal accruals, disciplined capital allocation and sustained deleveraging.

Prism RMC is pursuing a more disciplined project selection strategy in Mega Projects following the transition in its business model, alongside a rising share of value-added products in Commercial Concrete.

H & R Johnson will continue capacity optimisation and manufacturing modernisation - strategic upgrades at various plants plus plant rationalisation and operational optimisation - to improve capacity utilisation and cost competitiveness.
H & R Johnson will continue strengthening its premium product portfolio with higher contribution from GVT, large-format tiles and lifestyle-led bath solutions to support improved value realisations.
The bathware business is being grown through a distribution strategy that leverages H & R Johnson's core tiles distribution network alongside ongoing expansion of dedicated bathware channels.
